narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimates an 85% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning a high likelihood of difficulty repaying the loan as agreed. The most influential factor was the amount you requested. At 15,672 DM, it is far above the approved applicants’ average of about 3,020 DM, so the model saw a much heavier repayment burden. The second most important factor was the 48-month repayment period, compared with an approved average of about 19 months; a longer term increases uncertainty and total exposure. Third was your checking account status in the 0–200 DM range, which suggests limited financial buffer and pushed the prediction toward bad credit. All three top factors increased the risk estimate.

To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller amount and a shorter repayment period so the installments are more manageable. Strengthening your checking account balance and providing evidence of stable income or savings would also help. You could ask the bank about a smaller loan product or credit counseling, then reapply once your financial profile has improved.
